Messages.Author: Decebalus
Messages.Body:
I have a fundamental problem with the events. Its in the sense of the
events. What is the difference (apart from being played in the discard
phase) from events to master cards?

Both are played by a methuselah and often manipulate the whole
environment.

The new "government" type makes the missing difference very obviously.
Why is "Police Department" a master card and no government card (apart
that there was no events at that moment)?

If events would be real events, they had to reflect fundamental
changes that happen to the world (of that game) as a whole. But thats
not the case, because events are burned when the methuselah who played
them is ousted. Why should the Withering stop, when a methuselah dies?

I am not talking about games mechanics, i am talking about the logic
behind the game mechanic. What does the event reflect, that is not
reflected by master cards.

Messages.Author: Rogar
Messages.Body:
I think it was Decebalus <x5m...@gmx.de>, who once wrote:
> I have a fundamental problem with the events. Its in the sense of the
> events. What is the difference (apart from being played in the discard
> phase) from events to master cards? Both are played by a methuselah and
> often manipulate the whole environment.

But events do so more directly, and without discrimination. You could
say that (permanent) masters are assets that a methuselah may create or
gain control over, while events can only be set into motion, after which
the methuselah can only hope that his strategic planning will keep him
relatively unhindered by the effects of the unfolding event.

> The new "government" type makes the missing difference very obviously.
> Why is "Police Department" a master card and no government card (apart
> that there was no events at that moment)?

Because Police Department is not a general effect, but something the
methuselah has direct control over. He bribed or blackmailed or whatever
and can call upon the police for aid exactly when he wants to, if he
wants to.

However, I think there are some masters that would make more sense as
events these days. Anarch Revolt for instance.

> If events would be real events, they had to reflect fundamental
> changes that happen to the world (of that game) as a whole. But thats
> not the case, because events are burned when the methuselah who played
> them is ousted. Why should the Withering stop, when a methuselah dies?

You have a point here. It would make more sense for events to stay in
the game. However, I suspect that would have been too unbalancing.
There's already a lot of complaints about event decks that ruin the
game for the rest of the table, randomizing the outcome, and not
getting any VP's. Imagine that after ousting, the ten or so events
remained. Could even be something that was changed during play testing.

Anyway, I like events. When I was still into That Other Game, I liked
to build decks around global enchantments, to mess with the opponent's
game. When I switched to Vampire, I missed this style of deck building.
Now at last Vampire has a similar card type. Though I must admit my
attempts at a good event deck have not been successful as of yet. Ah,
well, we'll see what the future brings.

Rogar
